summary: The Boeing Co. stands as a leading global aerospace firm, dedicated to crafting both civilian jetliners and intricate defense, space, and security apparatus. Its extensive operations are segmented into four primary divisions. The Commercial Airplanes (BCA) unit is responsible for innovating, manufacturing, and selling its famous commercial jet aircraft, in addition to offering vital maintenance and support services to airlines across the globe. The Defense, Space and Security (BDS) segment delves into the research, creation, and enhancement of a wide array of military assets, including manned and unmanned combat aircraft and advanced weaponry like fighter jets, attack helicopters, and missile systems for global strike; transport solutions such as tanker, rotorcraft, and tilt-rotor aircraft; and sophisticated airborne surveillance and reconnaissance platforms for command, control, battle management, and anti-submarine warfare. Meanwhile, the Global Services (BGS) division provides an array of support and maintenance offerings to both its commercial and defense clientele. Lastly, Boeing Capital (BCC) plays a pivotal role in arranging the necessary financing for customers to acquire and take delivery of Boeing products, simultaneously managing the company's financial risk exposure. The enterprise was founded by William Edward Boeing on July 15, 1916, and is presently headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
